Timeline and ActivityFeed's marker reads the semantic `--<tone>-100` / `--<tone>-text` pair directly (Feed.jsx:65-69) — the SAME pair Card/Avatar/Callout read — and DELIBERATELY NOT the tone map StatusChip reads: StatusChip's own 2026-08-13 port moved to literal Tailwind stock-palette classes (bg-emerald-50/text-emerald-700 and friends), so a `danger` marker here and a `danger` StatusChip are close but no longer the exact same red — Feed.jsx's own file banner (lines 35-40) names this split on purpose, because Card/Avatar/Callout still agree with the token pair 3-to-1. Only success/warning/info/danger carry a fill; neutral is not a member of that set — an untoned or unrecognised tone falls back to `--ctl-raise`/`--ctl-fg-muted`, the same "nothing to say" pair Avatar's own untinted default reads. The rail itself is a single 1px `--ctl-track` line, centred behind a 30px marker column and stopping dead at the last item — "a trailing line reads as an event that failed to render" (Feed.jsx:164-168) — which replaces the old tiny-dot-on-a-`border-l` anatomy entirely rather than retinting it: a marker this size needs a track to sit on, not an edge to ride.

<ApprovalRow · ApprovalQueue/>

One item awaiting a decision — who, what, how long, and the two answers.

kit/Queue.jsx

This is the recipe the old cookbook called "Approval queue row", now a real component on both sides. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Queue.dc.html: the status chip and the new `decided` outcome pill are both built ON StatusChip (Chips.jsx) rather than a hand-rolled badge, so a row's colour and a register's status column agree by construction. `decided` is new — "approved" | "rejected" | undefined — and does NOT remove or reorder the row: it drops to opacity-60 and swaps the two buttons for a tone-tinted outcome chip (Check/success or X/danger), "so the person can see what they just did and the list does not jump under the cursor mid-review."

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
item.title string "Compressor seal failure" the row's subject line — truncates rather than wrapping, so a row is always one row
item.meta string "CLM-4417 · Marine · ₹4,20,000" the reference line, in the data voice — id, category, value. Not prose.
item.owner string "R. Iyer" draws an Avatar in the row's tone; initials are first + last. Omit it and the row starts at the title.
item.tone enum "warning" success · warning · info · danger · neutral (default). ONE tone drives the avatar, the status chip, and — when tone==="danger" — the age figure, together.
item.status string "At risk" the chip's label
item.age string "12d" how long it has waited, in the data voice — --danger-text only when tone=="danger", --ctl-fg otherwise. Hidden below sm — on a phone it is the first thing worth losing.
onApprove / onReject handler (item) => void each renders its button ONLY when supplied — no handler, no button, never a dead one
onOpen handler (item) => void makes ONLY the title a real <button> — never the row. Approve/Reject sit beside it as separate targets, so a decision can never also navigate.
decided "approved" | "rejected" "approved" NEW. Swaps the two buttons for a tone-tinted outcome StatusChip and drops the row to opacity-60. Does NOT remove or reorder the row, and does not replace the item's own status chip — both render.
actionLabels {approve,reject} { approve: "Grant", reject: "Decline" } the verbs belong to the domain: a claim is settled, a leave request is granted
items / empty array / string [] / "Nothing waiting on you." ApprovalQueue only. It owns the length check so every caller does not write it slightly differently.

a queue with both decisions wired — one tone per row drives the avatar and the status chip together

WHOLE-ROW CLICK WAS THE BUG THIS PASS FIXED, not a feature it protects. The pre-migration row made the ENTIRE row clickable whenever `onOpen` was supplied and then had to stopPropagation out of the Approve/Reject group to survive its own click target sitting inside a bigger one — exactly the anti-pattern this component's own "not a table row" argument warns against. Queue.dc.html settles it the other way: `onOpen` now lives ONLY on the title, rendered as its own reset <button>, never a wrapper around the row — a click anywhere else on the row does nothing at all, and no stopPropagation exists anywhere in Queue.jsx any more (Queue.jsx:31-40, 110-124). The row rule is `border-t border-ctl-raise first:border-0` — a border-TOP, not the old border-bottom — reusing the same --ctl-raise divider Card/WipStrip already read (Queue.jsx:103). A decided row keeps BOTH its own status chip (item.status) and the new outcome chip at once — the outcome doesn't replace the status, it reports the decision made about it.

<WipStrip/>

Per-stage counts against a cap — the band that leads a board page.

kit/Queue.jsx

The old cookbook's "WIP strip", now a component on both sides. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Queue.dc.html: the old freeform `alert` string ("2 > 7d") is GONE, replaced by a real numeric `cap` — a stage over its own cap turns the count's ink AND its bar --danger-600 and shows the fraction, "14/10"; under or at cap it's just the raw count. ONE STRIP, NOT A GRID OF CARDS: cells are joined with an inner --ctl-raise left-border, none on the first — the same seam Calendar.jsx's own grid cells use — so it wraps itself in `Card role="bare"` rather than each stage being its own shadow-sm Card in a gapped grid.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
stages array<{key,label,count,cap?,tone?}> { key: "raise", label: "Raise", count: 4, cap: 6, tone: "info" } one cell per stage, in board order, joined in a single strip — inner --ctl-raise rules between cells, none on the first
stages[].cap number 10 over cap: the count's ink AND the bar beneath it both switch to --danger-600, and the cap rides beside the count — "14/10". Under or at cap, just the raw count, no fraction shown.
stages[].tone enum "warning" colours only the small dot beside the label. Independent of cap — the count/bar colour comes from cap alone, never from tone.

four stages, one of them over cap ("In repair", 14/10 — tone="warning" colours only the dot, not the overage)

The aging note used to take the warning tone and never danger — that whole `alert` string is retired. Over cap now drives BOTH the count's ink and the bar fill to --danger-600 together (Queue.jsx:225-227, 240-244); `tone` is a SEPARATE, independent axis that colours only the small dot beside the label (Queue.jsx:200-204, 233-235) — a calm-toned stage can still run over cap, and does in the first specimen below (In repair: tone="warning", but the count and bar go danger because 14 > 10, not because of the tone). `flex`, not the old auto-fit grid: a strip that wraps to a second line breaks the shared-rule seam between cells, so cells stay in one row and the strip scrolls instead, the same trade-off Table.jsx makes for a wide table.

<KanbanBoard/>

Columns of cards — each stage a tinted well, and only the cards inside it lift.

kit/Board.jsx

[OURS] in all three languages the app has held. No design language declares a board; every doc renders a dashboard or a register. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Board.dc.html: "each stage is a tinted well in its own tone, so the board reads as stages at a glance — and the cards inside it are the only objects that lift." The card is drawn INLINE rather than composed from this kit's own Card — a geometry mismatch (14px padding / shadow-sm, a role Cards.jsx doesn't name) as much as a tone mismatch — and the owner avatar uses a LOCAL `initials()` and a stable name-hash tone, not Avatar.jsx's, because Avatar's Foundations tone vocabulary (success/warning/info/danger) doesn't compose with a board's Tailwind-native one. Presentational only: no drag, no drop, no reordering, and deliberately no grab cursor — "a board that looks draggable and is not is worse than one that plainly is not."

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
columns array<{key,label,tone?,items}> { key: "repair", label: "In repair", tone: "amber" } tone: a Tailwind palette name (rose/amber/sky/emerald/slate/blue/violet/teal/orange/indigo/gray) — omitted or unrecognised tones cycle the palette by column index rather than flattening to one colour.
columns[].items array<{id,title,note?,owner?,priority?,progress?,files?,comments?}> { id: "CLM-4417", title: "Compressor seal failure", note: "12 days open", priority: "High" } The cards. An empty array is a real state — the column keeps its heading and shows "Nothing here".
item.priority enum "High" High/Medium/Low, case-insensitive — drives the badge's OWN tone (rose/amber/blue), independent of the column's tone. Anything else falls back to slate.
item.owner string "M. Osei" Drives both the avatar's initials (first + last letter, Board's own local rule) and its tone — a stable hash of the name, so one person reads as one colour across every card, independent of the row's status.
item.progress number 0–100 55 A labelled bar. Value ink is --ctl-fg-muted at 0%, --ctl-fg in flight, and the Tailwind literal text-emerald-700 (not a token) at 100%.
item.files / item.comments number 2 Footer pills, rendered only when > 0.
onCardClick (item, column) => void (item, col) => open(item) Supplying it is the ONLY thing that makes a card respond — hover lift (-translate-y-0.5) + shadow-md + pointer cursor. Without it every card stays fully inert, per Board.dc.html's own "a panel that is not a target does not respond at all."

TONE VOCABULARY IS TAILWIND'S OWN, NOT FOUNDATIONS'. Every other tinted surface in this kit (StatusChip, Card's own `tone`, StatTile's delta pill) reads Foundations' 5-member semantic map (success/warning/info/danger/neutral). A board column can't: a stage's colour is picked per app by whoever configures the board — could be 5 stages, could be 8 — and 5 semantic tones doesn't have room for that, so column tone, priority-badge tone and owner-avatar tone all resolve through an 11-name Tailwind palette lookup instead (Board.jsx:68-90), completely unrelated to StatusChip's five. THE COLUMN IS NOT A CARD — still true, but satisfied differently now: the old cookbook column was fill-less entirely (`rounded-lg bg-muted/60`); this one IS tinted (`bg-<tone>-50`), and the separation from its white cards comes from tint-vs-shadow rather than no-fill-at-all — "white on a tint is the strongest card treatment available and it costs nothing" (Board.jsx:32-44). onCardClick uses Tailwind directly for its hover lift: `hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:shadow-md`.

Behaviour #cat-behaviour

<CountUp/>

A figure that animates to its value.

kit/Fx.jsx

The figure is one span; the behaviour is the component. In a prototype write the final figure straight into the span and animate it from your load script if you want the motion — the class list is what has to match, and it is two classes long. The two buttons carry the starter specimen's own outline and secondary ranks (Buttons.jsx's REDESIGNED pill geometry, not a legacy geometry bundle) so the row reads the same on both sides, but no snippet in this catalog ships a script tag: they are shape, not behaviour, and your load script is what makes them do anything. (Written as prose, not markup — the literal tag name here would trip the catalog's own no-scripts grep.)

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
value number 42 the target. In a prototype this is the SEED figure written out; the animation is optional chrome on top of it.
duration number 220 unset reads --motion-duration-move, so it matches every other moving thing in the language

the figure and its controls — the buttons are markup here; wire them in your load script

42

It reads the language's OWN move duration rather than a fixed 750ms, so a number settles at the same speed a bar grows — 220ms under Beacon, the language's own move duration. And it respects prefers-reduced-motion by jumping straight to the value, because an animated figure is decoration and decoration is the first thing that setting is asking you to drop. `tabular-nums` is not optional here: without it every tick re-measures the text and the number jitters sideways while it counts, which is the whole reason a proportional face is wrong for a figure.

<toast · Toaster/>

The confirmation that appears after an action, and the region it appears in.

kit/Fx.jsx

The shell already exposes `showToast(msg)` and a part should keep calling it — this entry is the ANATOMY, so the prototype's toast and the built app's Toaster are the same object rather than two designs that happen to share a verb. The region is bottom-centre, fixed, and pointer-events-none so it never eats a click meant for the page behind it; only the toast itself takes pointer events back.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
message string "Claim approved" the sentence. Past tense — a toast reports what happened, it does not promise.
tone enum "success" success · warning · info · danger · neutral — the same five StatusChip reads. `pending`/`strong` were dropped as status tones in Chips.jsx's redesign ("orange and near-black are actions here, not statuses").
ms number 4000 auto-dismiss. A toast carrying something the reader must act on is the wrong component — use Callout.

the region with one toast in it — fixed bottom-centre, and the region itself never eats a click

success Claim approved

The tone chip inside the toast is a real StatusChip, sharing the same five tones — so a toast saying "Approved" and a status column saying "Approved" are the same colour in every language. That is the point of reusing it rather than giving the toast its own palette. The surface reads `shadow-md`, not `shadow-sm`: a toast genuinely floats over the page, which is the same rung Modal takes.

<CustomEmbed/>

An external page in an iframe. The card is ours; what is inside it is not.

kit/Fx.jsx

The surrounding card follows the language exactly as every other card does. The CONTENT does not and cannot: an embedded third-party page paints its own tiles, controls and typography inside a document we do not style. Being honest about that boundary is the whole design of this component.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
src string "about:blank" nothing renders without it
title string "Embed placeholder" the iframe's accessible name — a frame with no title is an unlabelled document to a screen reader
height number 140 pixels, written straight into style
sandbox string "allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms" narrow on purpose; widening it is a security decision, not a layout one

against about:blank — a catalog page should not reach the network

markup 
<iframe src="about:blank" title="Embed placeholder" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms"
        class="border border-edge w-full rounded-lg bg-card" style="height: 140px"></iframe>

The sandbox is narrow ON PURPOSE — scripts, same-origin and forms, nothing else. An embed that can script its parent is a hole in the app, and the default when you omit `sandbox` entirely is no sandbox at all. Rendered against `about:blank` in this catalog because a catalog page should not reach the network; that is the same rule PhotoCard's specimens follow.

<StoresMap/>

Locations as a themed list rather than an embedded map.

kit/Fx.jsx

A deliberate departure, and the reasoning is the same one CustomEmbed makes from the other side. The legacy component embedded a map provider. An embedded third-party map is the one thing in either kit that CANNOT follow the design language at all — it paints its own tiles, labels and controls inside an iframe nobody styles, a flat grey Mercator hole in an otherwise on-brand page no matter what the surrounding language looks like.

locations array<{id,name,address}> { id: 1, name: "Home Center", address: "12 Harbour Road, Marine District" } name in the ordinary ink, address in the meta ink; both truncate
onSelect handler (location) => void renders the Open button and is where a caller wires a real map. No handler, no button.

A list that themes correctly is more honest than a map that never will. It reads the same row geometry Table and ApprovalRow read (`px-5 py-3 gap-4`, `border-row-divider`), so a location list beside a register lines up with it. `onSelect` is where a caller wires a real map if the app genuinely needs one — the component's job is to be the themed half.
